Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 1–5:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The Most Merciful (1) taught the Qur'an (2), created man (3), taught him eloquent speech (4), the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning (5)﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: "The Most Merciful, O people, out of His mercy toward you, taught you the Qur'an. Thus He bestowed this blessing upon you, when He made clear to you what pleases your Lord and informed you of what provokes His wrath, so that you might obey Him by following what pleases Him from you, by acting on what He has commanded you, and by avoiding what displeases Him, so that you may thereby merit His abundant reward and be saved from His painful punishment."

It has been related from Qatadah concerning this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqayli narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam al-Ajli narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he said, concerning the interpretation of ﴿The Most Merciful taught the Qur'an﴾: "It is a great blessing, by Allah."

* *

And His saying: ﴿created man﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: He created Adam, who is "man", according to some of them.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿created man﴾, he said: "Man" is Adam.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿created man﴾, he said: "Man" is Adam (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, by this He means all of mankind, and He used the singular in the wording only because it expresses its kind, as it is said: ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾. Both opinions are not far from the truth, since the apparent meaning of the speech allows for both.

* *

And His saying: ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: He taught man eloquent speech.

Then the interpreters differed regarding what is meant by "al-bayan" (eloquent speech) in this place. Some of them said: It means the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾: Allah taught him the explanation of this world and the Hereafter, clarifying what is lawful and unlawful for him, so that He might establish proof against His creation through it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾: the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, so that He might establish proof against him through it.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾, he said: "Good and evil were made clear to him, and what he should do and what he should leave."

Others said: It means speech, i.e., that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, taught man speech.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾: "Al-bayan is speech."

The correct view on this matter is to say: The meaning of that is that Allah taught man what he needs of the affairs of his religion and his worldly life, of the lawful and the unlawful, of livelihood and of speech, and other things he needs. For the Mighty and Majestic did not restrict His statement to teaching him some kinds of eloquence and not others; rather He stated it in general terms, saying: "He taught him eloquent speech," so it is as general as He, the Mighty and Majestic, made it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: Its meaning: the sun and the moon [run] by reckoning, and by stations for them, which they traverse and do not exceed.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Sammak ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "By calculation and stations through which they move."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "They run by number and reckoning."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Malik, ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "By calculation and stations."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾: i.e., by calculation and term.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "They run in calculation."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾: "By them time and periods are reckoned. Were it not for the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, no one would know how to reckon anything, even if the age were all night, how would one reckon, or all day, how would one reckon."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "By calculation and term."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they run according to a measure.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Abu al-Sahba', from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "They run by a measure."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they revolve like the pivot of a millstone.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya narrated to us, from Mujahid, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿with a reckoning﴾, he said: "Like the hasban of the millstone" (the pivot).

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿with a reckoning﴾, he said: "Like the hasban of the millstone."

The most correct of these opinions is the view of the one who said: its meaning is that the sun and the moon run by reckoning and stations, because ḥusbān (reckoning) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I reckoned it, a reckoning (ḥisāb) and a reckoning (ḥusbān)," like their saying: "I disbelieved it, a disbelieving (kufrān)," and "I forgave him, a forgiving (ghufrān)." It has also been said that it is the plural of ḥisāb, just as shuhbān is the plural of shihāb.

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding what the words "the sun and the moon" are in the nominative case governed by. Some of them said: They are in the nominative by ḥusbān, i.e., by ḥisāb, and the predicate is omitted; he said: "I think, and Allah knows best, that he said: they run by reckoning." Some of those who rejected this view among them said: "This is an error; ḥusbān does not govern the sun and the moon in the nominative, i.e., 'they are by reckoning.' He said: the statement then becomes: 'He taught him eloquent speech: that the sun and the moon are by reckoning.' He said: the verb is not omitted and left implied except rarely in speech."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾, he said: "Good and evil were made clear to him, and what he should do and what he should leave."

Others said: It means speech, i.e., that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, taught man speech.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿taught him eloquent speech﴾: "Al-bayan is speech."

The correct view on this matter is to say: The meaning of that is that Allah taught man what he needs of the affairs of his religion and his worldly life, of the lawful and the unlawful, of livelihood and of speech, and other things he needs. * *

And His saying: ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: Its meaning: the sun and the moon [run] by reckoning, and by stations for them, which they traverse and do not exceed.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Sammak ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "By calculation and stations through which they move."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they run according to a measure.

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Abu al-Sahba', from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying ﴿the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾, he said: "They run by a measure."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they revolve like the pivot of a millstone.

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya narrated to us, from Mujahid, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿with a reckoning﴾, he said: "Like the hasban of the millstone" (the pivot).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 1–5:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The Most Merciful (1) taught the Qur'an (2), created man (3), taught him eloquent speech (4), the sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning (5)﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: "The Most Merciful, O people, out of His mercy toward you, taught you the Qur'an. Thus He bestowed this blessing upon you, when He made clear to you what pleases your Lord and informed you of what provokes His wrath, so that you might obey Him by following what pleases Him from you, by acting on what He has commanded you, and by avoiding what displeases Him, so that you may thereby merit His abundant reward and be saved from His painful punishment."

It has been related from Qatadah concerning this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqayli narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam al-Ajli narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he said, concerning the interpretation of ﴿The Most Merciful taught the Qur'an﴾: "It is a great blessing, by Allah."

* *

And His saying: ﴿created man﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: He created Adam, who is "man", according to some of them.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿created man﴾, he said: "Man" is Adam.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿created man﴾, he said: "Man" is Adam (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 6–9:

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of "al-najm" (the star, or low-growing plant) in this passage, while agreeing that "al-shajar" (trees) refers to that which stands upon a stem. Some of them said: By "al-najm" in this place is meant the vegetation that sprouts from the earth and spreads upon it, and does not stand on a stalk, such as herbs and the like.

Those who said this:

• ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾, he said: That which spreads over the earth.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding His words: ﴿And the star﴾, he said: "The star" is everything that goes flat upon the earth, spread out; and the Arabs call the herb (thabil) "najm."

• Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalani narrated to me, saying: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Sharik, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾, he said: "The star" is the vegetation of the earth.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿And the star﴾, he said: "The star" is that which has no stalk.

Others said: By "al-najm" in this place is meant the star of the sky.

Those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And the star﴾, he said: The star of the sky.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿And the star﴾, meaning: the star of the sky.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾, he said: He only means the star.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, similarly.

The most correct of the two opinions in this matter is the view of those who said: By "al-najm" is meant what sprouts from the earth of plants, so that "al-shajar" is joined to it by way of coordination. Thus its meaning, on this basis, is that whatever stands upon a stalk and whatever does not stand upon a stalk both prostrate to God, meaning that all things of differing forms among His creation prostrate to Him. This is more fitting and more appropriate to the meaning of the speech than other interpretations. As for His words ﴿And the tree﴾, the tree is that whose description has already been given.

The exegetes said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

• ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the tree prostrate﴾, he said: "The tree" is everything that stands upon a stalk.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding His words: ﴿And the tree﴾, he said: "The tree" is everything that stands upon a stalk.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿And the tree﴾, he said: "The tree" is the trees of the earth.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿And the tree prostrate﴾, he said: "The tree" is that which has a trunk (suwuq).

As for His words ﴿prostrate﴾, it means the prostration of their shadows, as the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows [prostrate] in the mornings and the evenings﴾.

As:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn ʿAbd al-Mu'min narrated to us, from Zubruqan, from Abu Razin and Saʿid, regarding ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾, they both said: Their shadows are their prostration.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾: Nothing of His creation descends from the sky except that He makes it a servant to Him, willingly or unwillingly.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, and this is also the view of Qatada.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾, he said: It prostrates morning and evening.

It was said: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾ uses the dual form, though it reports about two groups.

al-Farra' claimed that when the Arabs join two plural groups of non-human things, such as the lote-tree (sidr) and the palm, they treat their verb as singular, saying: "The sheep and the camels has come," and "The palm and the lote-tree has been watered." He said: This is most of their speech, and using the dual is permissible.

* *

As for His words ﴿And the heaven He raised﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the heaven He raised above the earth.

* *

As for His words ﴿And He set the balance﴾:

He says: And He placed justice among His creation on the earth.

It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud) it is ﴿khafada al-mizan﴾ (He lowered the balance), and "lowering" and "setting" are close in meaning in the speech of the Arabs.

The exegetes said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And He set the balance﴾, he said: Justice.

* *

As for His words ﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: That you not wrong and diminish in weighing.

As:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾: Be just, O son of Adam, as you wish to be treated justly, and give full measure as you wish to be given full measure, for the welfare of people lies in justice.

Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: O assembly of the mawali (non-Arab clients), you have been entrusted with two matters by which those before you were destroyed: the measure and the balance.

• ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Muʿawiya narrated to us, from Mughira, from Muslim, from Abu al-Mughira, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say in the market of Medina: O assembly of the mawali, you have been tested with two matters by which two nations among the nations were destroyed: the mikyal (measure) and the mizan (balance).

• He said: Marwan narrated to us, from Mughira, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas saw a man weighing and tilting the scale, so he said: Straighten the tongue (of the balance), straighten the tongue! Has not God said: ﴿And establish the weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾?

* *

As for His words ﴿And establish the weight with justice﴾:

He says: And set the tongue of the balance straight with justice.

* *

As for His words ﴿And do not make deficient the balance﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And do not reduce the weight when you weigh for people, wronging them.

The exegetes said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And the heaven He raised and He set the balance. That you not transgress in the balance. And establish the weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾. Qatada said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: O assembly of the mawali, you have been entrusted with two matters by which those before you were destroyed: a man who fears God at his balance, a man who fears God at his measure, for only a little thing is lost by it, and it does not diminish him; rather God will increase him, if He wills.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And establish the weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾: To reduce it is to make it deficient; "making deficient" (takhsir) is its reduction.

The majority of the readers of Madina and Basra, and some of the Makkans and some of the Kufans, recited it in the nominative (*raf'*), as a conjunction to *al-habb* (the grain), meaning: "And therein is the grain with its *'asf*, and therein is also the *rayhan*." The majority of the Kufan readers recited ﴿wa-r-rayhani﴾ in the genitive (*khafd*), as a conjunction to *al-'asf*, meaning: "and the grain with its *'asf* and with its *rayhan*." [[This is from the words of al-Farra' in *Ma'ani al-Qur'an*, page 320 of the manuscript.]]

The most correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recited it in the genitive, for the reason which I have explained in its interpretation, and that it means provision. As for those who recited it in the nominative, they directed its interpretation, in my view, to mean the fragrant plant which is smelled; for this reason they chose the nominative in it. Its being in the genitive, meaning "therein is the grain with its leaf and straw, and with its provision that is eaten," is more fitting and better, for what we have already explained before.

The Exalted said: ﴿And the earth — He laid it out for the creatures﴾. That is, He spread it out for creation, and they are the *anam* (creatures).

We say, in this matter, what the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿li-l-anam﴾: "for the creation."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And the earth — He laid it out for the creatures﴾: "Everything that has a soul."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And the earth — He laid it out for the creatures﴾: "For creation: the jinn and the humans."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿li-l-anam﴾: "For the creatures."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿li-l-anam﴾: "For the creation."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿wa-d'aha li-l-anam﴾: "The *anam* are the creation."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the earth — He laid it out for the creatures﴾: "For the creation."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, the same.

As for His words ﴿Therein is fruit, and the palm trees with sheaths﴾: The Exalted said: In the earth is fruit; the *ha'* and *alif* in *fiha* refer back to the earth. ﴿And the palm trees with sheaths﴾: *al-akmam* is the plural of *kimm*, which is that in which something is enclosed.

The people of *ta'wil* differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: It refers to the palm's enclosure within its fibres.

Those who said that:

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I asked al-Hasan about His words ﴿wa-n-nakhlu dhatu l-akmam﴾, and he said: "A frond of fibre which is wrapped around it."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and al-Hasan: ﴿dhat al-akmam﴾: "Its *akmam* are its fibre."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the palm trees with sheaths﴾: "The fibre that is upon them."

Others said: By *al-akmam* is meant the *rufat* (the husks, or the shrivelled remains).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the palm trees with sheaths﴾, he said: "Its *akmam* are its *rufat*."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of the statement is: and the palm trees bearing the spathe (*tal'*) enclosed in its sheath.

Those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And the palm trees with sheaths﴾, and it was said to him: "It is the spathe?" He said: "Yes, and it is enclosed within a sheath until it bursts open from it." He said: "And the grain also is in sheaths." And he recited: ﴿And no fruits come out of their sheaths﴾ [41:47].

The most correct of these opinions is to say: God described the palm trees as having sheaths; they are enclosed in their fibre, and their spathe is enclosed in its sheath. God did not restrict the report about them to their being enclosed in their fibre, nor to the enclosure of their spathe in its sheath; rather, He made the report general, saying that they have sheaths.

So the correct view is to say: It is meant that they have fibre in which they are enclosed, and that they have a spathe which is enclosed in its sheath; so it is generalised, just as His Majesty generalised it.

* *

As for His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾:

The Exalted said: And therein is the grain, namely the grain of wheat and barley, which has leaves; and the straw is the *'asf*, and it is what 'Alqama ibn 'Abada meant when he said:

*They water the channels, whose 'asif has inclined,*
*its lower part from the flowing water, which is filled.* [[This verse is one of the examples cited by Abu 'Ubayda in *Majaz al-Qur'an* (leaf 172 of the Cairo University photograph no. 26390, from the "Murad Mulla" manuscript; our references to the first photograph no. 26059 had ended, as its leaves end at Surat al-Qamar). Abu 'Ubayda recited it at His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾, saying: "It brings forth a *'asifa*, which is its covering at the top; and it is the *hubud*, and its *udhn* is merely its increase and abundance, and its leaf which is *ya'safu* (stripped). It is as 'Alqama ibn 'Abada said: 'They water the channels...' (the verse)."

*Tamma*: he filled it; nothing was left in it; and "tamma his vessel" means he filled it. The commentator of *Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili* (p. 426) said: *al-madhanib* is the plural of *madhnab*, the course by which water flows to the ground; the stream flows from the meadow with its water to its... *'asifatuha* is the leaf which is cut and eaten, and then its root is watered so that its leaves return. *Judhuruha* is that which descends from these channels and settles. *Al-atiyy* is the stream; and he meant by it here what flows of water in the stream. *Al-matmum* is that which is full of water.]]

The people of *ta'wil* said the same as we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾: "Straw."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾: "*Al-'asf* is the leaf of the green crop whose tops have been cut; it is called *'asf* when it dries."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id: ﴿And the grain with its husk﴾: "Green herbage from the crop."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk﴾: "Its *'asf* is its straw."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: "*Al-'asf* is the straw."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And the grain with its husk﴾: "The grain is wheat and barley, and the *'asf* is the straw."

- Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Malik regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾: "The grain is what first sprouts."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾: "*Al-'asf* is the leaf of everything. It is said of the crop when it is cut: *'asafa*, and every leaf is *'asafa*."

- al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq 'Atiyya ibn al-Harith narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk﴾: "*Al-'asf* is the straw."

- Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sallat narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿dhu l-'asf﴾: "*Al-'asf* is the crop."

Some of them said: *Al-'asf* is the grain of wheat and barley itself.

Those who said that:

- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plant﴾: "As for *al-'asf*, it is wheat and barley."

As for His words ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾, the people of *ta'wil* differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: It is provision (*rizq*).

Those who said that:

- Zayd ibn Akhzam al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Amir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, saying: 'Utba ibn Yaqzan narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Every *rayhan* in the Qur'an is provision."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The provision."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The provision; and some of them say: *rayhanana*" (our sustenance).

- Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sallat narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The wind."

- al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq 'Atiyya ibn al-Harith narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The provision and the food."

Others said: It is the fragrant plant which is smelled.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "*Al-rayhan* is what the earth produces of fragrant plants."

- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "As for the fragrant plant, it is what the earth produces of fragrant plants."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾, he said: "Your fragrant plant, this." Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The fragrant plants whose scent is found."

Others said: It is the greenness of the crop.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾: "The greenness of the crop."

Others said: It is that which stands upon a stalk.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "*Al-rayhan* is that which stands upon a stalk."

The most correct of these opinions is the view of the one who said: It is meant as provision, which is the grain that is eaten from it.

We only say that this is the most correct view because God, may His majesty be exalted, informed us that the grain has *'asf*, which is the leaves that arise from it, and the straw when it dries. So the more fitting meaning of *rayhan* is that its grain which arises from it should be meant, since it is of the same kind as that from which the *'asf* comes. It is also heard from the Arabs saying: "We went out seeking the *rayhan* of God and His provision," and they say: "*Subhanaka wa-rayhanaka*," meaning: "and your provision." And from this is the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:

*Peace of God, and His rayhan, and His Garden, and a bountiful sky.* [[The verse is by al-Namir ibn Tawlab al-'Ukli (*Lisan*: *rawh*), and after it:

*A cloud that sends down the provision of the servants, and revives the lands, and the trees become good.*

It is among the examples cited by Abu 'Ubayda in *Majaz al-Qur'an* (leaf 172 of photograph 26390 at Cairo University), where he said: "*Al-rayhan* and the grain from it which is eaten: it is said *subhanaka wa-rayhanaka*, meaning your provision. Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said: 'Peace of God...' (the verse)." End. In *Lisan* (*darr*): "*Al-durra* in rains is that one follows another, and its plural is *durar*; and the cloud has *durar*, meaning it pours; the plural is *durar*. Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said: ...the two verses." "A bountiful sky" means one having *durar*. End.]]

It was reported from some of them that he used to say: "*Al-'asf* is the eaten grain; and *al-rayhan* is the healthy one which has not been eaten."

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿wa-r-rayhanu﴾. The majority of the readers of Madina and Basra, and some of the Makkans and some of the Kufans, recited it in the nominative (*raf'*), as a conjunction to *al-habb* (the grain), meaning: "And therein is the grain with its *'asf*, and therein is also the *rayhan*." The majority of the Kufan readers recited ﴿wa-r-rayhani﴾ in the genitive (*khafd*), as a conjunction to *al-'asf*, meaning: "and the grain with its *'asf* and with its *rayhan*." [[This is from the words of al-Farra' in *Ma'ani al-Qur'an*, page 320 of the manuscript.]]

The most correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recited it in the genitive, for the reason which I have explained in its interpretation, and that it means provision. As for those who recited it in the nominative, they directed its interpretation, in my view, to mean the fragrant plant which is smelled; for this reason they chose the nominative in it. Its being in the genitive, meaning "therein is the grain with its leaf and straw, and with its provision that is eaten," is more fitting and better, for what we have already explained before.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 13–16:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny? (13) He created man from clay like pottery, (14) and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. (15) So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny? (16)﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says by His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: So which of the bounties of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, will you deny among these bounties?

As related:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sahl al-Sarraj narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: So which blessing of your Lord will you both deny?

ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ He said: "No, by any of them, O Lord."

* Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Musa and ʿAmr ibn Malik al-Nadri narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, from Nafi', from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Rahman, or it was recited in his presence, and he said: "What is the matter with me that I hear the jinn give a better answer to their Lord than you do?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Whenever I came to the saying of Allah: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, the jinn would say: 'No, by any of the bounties of our Lord do we deny.'"

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, meaning: So which blessing of God will you both deny?

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, meaning, to the jinn and humankind: So which of the blessings of God will you both deny?

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash and others, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that when he recited ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ he would say: "No, by any of them, our Lord."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: "The ala' (favours) is power. So by which of His powers will you both deny that He created your such-and-such? By which power of God will you both deny, O two weighty ones, the jinn and humankind?"

If someone says to us: How is it said, ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, addressing two, when at the beginning of the statement only one is mentioned, namely man? It is said: The address in His saying ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ returns to man and the jinn. What follows this speech indicates that this is so, namely His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.﴾ It has also been said: The speech was made into an address to two, although the report began about one, because of an established practice of the Arabs, who address one person with the verb of two, saying: "Leave them (dual), O boy," and similar things, which we have explained in this book in other places.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: God created man, namely Adam, from ṣalṣāl, which is dry clay that has not been fired; because of its dryness, it makes a clattering sound when struck and tapped, like pottery. That is, because of its dryness, even though it has not been fired, it is like that which has been baked in fire, so it clatters as pottery clatters. Al-fakhkhar is clay that has been baked with fire.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* ʿUbayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Muslim, meaning al-Mala'i, narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from clay like pottery﴾: He said: It is from the clay which, when the sky has rained and the earth has dried, becomes like thin potsherds.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿAmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created Adam from clay that is lazib (sticky), and al-lazib is the sticky, good (clay) after black mud, molded and foul-smelling.

He said: It was only black molded mud after the earth. He said: So He created Adam with His hand. He said: He remained forty nights as a body lying prone, and Iblis would come to him and strike him with his foot, and it would clatter and make a sound. He said: That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿like pottery﴾, meaning: like a thing that is hollow and not solid.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id and ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Battin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ṣalṣāl is finely pounded dust.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ṣalṣāl is finely pounded dust.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, meaning: dry clay.

* Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrima, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, who said: ṣalṣāl is clay mixed with sand, so it became like pottery.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾: ṣalṣāl is dry dust which makes a clattering sound, so it is like pottery, as God, Mighty and Majestic, said.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, who said: From clay that has a clattering sound, being dry; then He created man from it.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, said: Adam dried in the clay in Paradise until it became like ṣalṣāl, which is pottery; and ḥama' masnun is foul-smelling mud.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, who said: From dry dust that has a clattering sound.

* He said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Shabib narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, who said: It is what is pressed and comes out between the fingers. And if someone were to interpret the word ṣalṣāl as being of the form fa'lal from their saying ṣalla al-lahm (when meat has rotted and its smell has changed), just as it is said ṣarra al-bab, becoming ṣarṣar, and kabkaba from kabba, that would be a valid and acceptable view.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: He created the jinn from marij of fire, which is that whose parts are mixed one with another, among red, yellow and green, from their saying marija amr al-qawm when the affair of the people became confused; and from the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "How will you be when you are among a worthless remnant of people, whose covenants and trusts have become confused! That is the blaze of the fire and its tongue."

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri Abu Hafs narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Muslim narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: From its middle and best part.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, meaning: He created him from the flame of fire, from the best of fire.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, meaning: pure fire.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿAmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from marij of fire, which is the tongue of fire that appears at its edge when it is kindled.

* Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrima, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: From the best of fire.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: The yellow and green flame that rises over the fire when it is kindled.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾: The marij is the flame.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, who said: From a flame of fire.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: So which of the bounties of your Lord, O two weighty ones, will you deny among these bounties?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 13–16:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny? (13) He created man from clay like pottery, (14) and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. (15) So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny? (16)﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says by His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: So which of the bounties of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, will you deny among these bounties?

As related:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sahl al-Sarraj narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: So which blessing of your Lord will you both deny?

ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ He said: "No, by any of them, O Lord."

* Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Musa and ʿAmr ibn Malik al-Nadri narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, from Nafi', from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Rahman, or it was recited in his presence, and he said: "What is the matter with me that I hear the jinn give a better answer to their Lord than you do?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Whenever I came to the saying of Allah: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, the jinn would say: 'No, by any of the bounties of our Lord do we deny.'"

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, meaning: So which blessing of God will you both deny?

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, meaning, to the jinn and humankind: So which of the blessings of God will you both deny?

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash and others, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that when he recited ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ he would say: "No, by any of them, our Lord."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾: "The ala' (favours) is power. So by which of His powers will you both deny that He created your such-and-such? By which power of God will you both deny, O two weighty ones, the jinn and humankind?"

If someone says to us: How is it said, ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾, addressing two, when at the beginning of the statement only one is mentioned, namely man? It is said: The address in His saying ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ returns to man and the jinn. What follows this speech indicates that this is so, namely His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.﴾ It has also been said: The speech was made into an address to two, although the report began about one, because of an established practice of the Arabs, who address one person with the verb of two, saying: "Leave them (dual), O boy," and similar things, which we have explained in this book in other places.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: God created man, namely Adam, from ṣalṣāl, which is dry clay that has not been fired; because of its dryness, it makes a clattering sound when struck and tapped, like pottery. That is, because of its dryness, even though it has not been fired, it is like that which has been baked in fire, so it clatters as pottery clatters. Al-fakhkhar is clay that has been baked with fire.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* ʿUbayd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Muslim, meaning al-Mala'i, narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from clay like pottery﴾: He said: It is from the clay which, when the sky has rained and the earth has dried, becomes like thin potsherds.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿAmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created Adam from clay that is lazib (sticky), and al-lazib is the sticky, good (clay) after black mud, molded and foul-smelling.

He said: It was only black molded mud after the earth. He said: So He created Adam with His hand. He said: He remained forty nights as a body lying prone, and Iblis would come to him and strike him with his foot, and it would clatter and make a sound. He said: That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿like pottery﴾, meaning: like a thing that is hollow and not solid.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id and ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Battin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ṣalṣāl is finely pounded dust.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ṣalṣāl is finely pounded dust.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, meaning: dry clay.

* Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrima, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, who said: ṣalṣāl is clay mixed with sand, so it became like pottery.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾: ṣalṣāl is dry dust which makes a clattering sound, so it is like pottery, as God, Mighty and Majestic, said.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, who said: From clay that has a clattering sound, being dry; then He created man from it.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, said: Adam dried in the clay in Paradise until it became like ṣalṣāl, which is pottery; and ḥama' masnun is foul-smelling mud.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, who said: From dry dust that has a clattering sound.

* He said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Shabib narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, who said: It is what is pressed and comes out between the fingers. And if someone were to interpret the word ṣalṣāl as being of the form fa'lal from their saying ṣalla al-lahm (when meat has rotted and its smell has changed), just as it is said ṣarra al-bab, becoming ṣarṣar, and kabkaba from kabba, that would be a valid and acceptable view.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: He created the jinn from marij of fire, which is that whose parts are mixed one with another, among red, yellow and green, from their saying marija amr al-qawm when the affair of the people became confused; and from the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "How will you be when you are among a worthless remnant of people, whose covenants and trusts have become confused! That is the blaze of the fire and its tongue."

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Jubayri Abu Hafs narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Muslim narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: From its middle and best part.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, meaning: He created him from the flame of fire, from the best of fire.

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, meaning: pure fire.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿAmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from marij of fire, which is the tongue of fire that appears at its edge when it is kindled.

* Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrima, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: From the best of fire.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: The yellow and green flame that rises over the fire when it is kindled.

* And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: and the red.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, who said: It is the cut-off red flame.

* He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, who said: The best of fire.

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿from marij of fire﴾: From the flame of fire.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾: That is, from the flame of fire.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿from marij of fire﴾, who said: From the flame of fire.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾: The marij is the flame.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and He created the jinn from marij of fire﴾, who said: From a flame of fire.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

God, the One who is mentioned, says: So which of the bounties of your Lord, O two weighty ones, will you deny among these bounties?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 17–21:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾ (17) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (18) ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾ (19) ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ (20) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: That is your Lord, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, i.e. jinn and mankind), ﴿Lord of the two Easts﴾. By "the two Easts" is meant the rising-point of the sun in winter and its rising-point in summer.

* *

And His words: ﴿and Lord of the two Wests﴾

That is: and the Lord of the setting-point of the sun in winter and its setting-point in summer.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-points of summer and the setting-points of summer. Two risings in which the sun travels through three hundred and sixty callings (buruj), for each buruj there is a rising; it does not rise from the same place two days running. And in the West there are three hundred and sixty buruj, for each buruj there is a setting; it does not set in the same buruj two days running."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-point of winter and its setting-point, and the rising-point of summer and its setting-point."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾: "Its rising-point in winter and its rising-point in summer."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-point of winter and its setting-point, and the rising-point of summer and its setting-point."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The shortest rising-point in the year and the longest rising-point in the year, and the shortest setting-point in the year and the longest setting-point in the year."

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

That is: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, would you deny, from among these blessings He has bestowed upon you, by His subjecting the sun for you in these two risings and two settings, running for both of you constantly for your benefit and for the welfare of your worldly life and your livelihood?

* *

And His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Lord of the two Easts and the Lord of the two Wests released the two seas, meeting side by side. By His words ﴿released (maraja)﴾ is meant: sent forth and let loose, from the saying: "Fulan released his beast (marraja fulan dabbatahu)" when he let it loose and left it.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas﴾, he says: "He sent forth."

The people of knowledge differed concerning the two seas mentioned by Allah, may His praise be exalted, in this verse: which two seas are they? Some said: They are two seas: one in the heaven and the other on the earth.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side * Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and a sea on the earth."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and a sea on the earth."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and in the earth, meeting each year."

Others said: What is meant is the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad, client of Mus'ab, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "The Sea of Rome, and the Sea of Persia and Yemen."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾: "The two seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "The Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome."

The most correct of the sayings in my view is the saying of those who said: What is meant is the sea of the heaven and the sea of the earth, because Allah said: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, and pearls and coral come forth only from the shells of the sea of the earth, from the drops of rain of the heaven. So it is known that this refers to the sea of the earth and the sea of the heaven.

* *

And His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Between them is a partition and a separation, so that neither of them corrupts the other, and so that neither transgresses against the other by that. Among the Arabs, everything that lies between two things is a barrier (barzakh), and what lies between this world and the Hereafter is a barzakh.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses against the other."

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "Between them is a partition from Allah, so neither transgresses against the other."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he says: "A partition."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, and the barzakh: "This island, this dry land."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "The barzakh between them is the land that lies between them."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "The salt is restrained from the sweet, and the sweet from the salt, and the water from the dry land, and the dry land from the water, so that neither of them transgresses upon the other by its strength, its subtlety and its power."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side * Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "He prevented them from meeting by the barrier He placed between them from the earth." He said: "The barzakh is what lies beyond the land which He placed between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾. Some said: The meaning of that is: neither of them transgresses against the other.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses against the other."

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that they do not mix.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "They do not mix."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they do not transgress upon the dry land.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Upon the dry land. Whatever one takes from the other is transgression, so Allah restrains each from the other by His power, subtlety and majesty, blessed and exalted is He."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: they do not transgress by meeting.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses by wanting to meet its companion."

The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in my view, is to say: Allah described the two seas mentioned in this verse as not transgressing, and He did not restrict their description to one thing rather than another, but made the report about them general. So the correct approach is to generalize it as Allah, exalted is His praise, generalized it: it is said that they do not transgress upon anything, neither does one of them transgress upon the other, nor do they exceed the limit which Allah has set for them.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So which of the blessings of Allah your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, would you deny, from among these blessings He has bestowed upon you, by His releasing the two seas, until He made for you by that an adornment which you wear.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 17–21:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾ (17) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (18) ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾ (19) ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ (20) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: That is your Lord, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, i.e. jinn and mankind), ﴿Lord of the two Easts﴾. By "the two Easts" is meant the rising-point of the sun in winter and its rising-point in summer.

* *

And His words: ﴿and Lord of the two Wests﴾

That is: and the Lord of the setting-point of the sun in winter and its setting-point in summer.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-points of summer and the setting-points of summer. Two risings in which the sun travels through three hundred and sixty callings (buruj), for each buruj there is a rising; it does not rise from the same place two days running. And in the West there are three hundred and sixty buruj, for each buruj there is a setting; it does not set in the same buruj two days running."
