He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "Between them is a partition from Allah, so neither transgresses against the other."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he says: "A partition."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, and the barzakh: "This island, this dry land."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "The barzakh between them is the land that lies between them."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "The salt is restrained from the sweet, and the sweet from the salt, and the water from the dry land, and the dry land from the water, so that neither of them transgresses upon the other by its strength, its subtlety and its power."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side * Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "He prevented them from meeting by the barrier He placed between them from the earth." He said: "The barzakh is what lies beyond the land which He placed between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾. Some said: The meaning of that is: neither of them transgresses against the other.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses against the other."

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that they do not mix.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "They do not mix."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they do not transgress upon the dry land.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Upon the dry land. Whatever one takes from the other is transgression, so Allah restrains each from the other by His power, subtlety and majesty, blessed and exalted is He."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: they do not transgress by meeting.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses by wanting to meet its companion."

The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in my view, is to say: Allah described the two seas mentioned in this verse as not transgressing, and He did not restrict their description to one thing rather than another, but made the report about them general. So the correct approach is to generalize it as Allah, exalted is His praise, generalized it: it is said that they do not transgress upon anything, neither does one of them transgress upon the other, nor do they exceed the limit which Allah has set for them.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So which of the blessings of Allah your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, would you deny, from among these blessings He has bestowed upon you, by His releasing the two seas, until He made for you by that an adornment which you wear.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 17–21:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾ (17) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (18) ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾ (19) ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ (20) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: That is your Lord, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, i.e. jinn and mankind), ﴿Lord of the two Easts﴾. By "the two Easts" is meant the rising-point of the sun in winter and its rising-point in summer.

* *

And His words: ﴿and Lord of the two Wests﴾

That is: and the Lord of the setting-point of the sun in winter and its setting-point in summer.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-points of summer and the setting-points of summer. Two risings in which the sun travels through three hundred and sixty callings (buruj), for each buruj there is a rising; it does not rise from the same place two days running. And in the West there are three hundred and sixty buruj, for each buruj there is a setting; it does not set in the same buruj two days running."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-point of winter and its setting-point, and the rising-point of summer and its setting-point."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾: "Its rising-point in winter and its rising-point in summer."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The rising-point of winter and its setting-point, and the rising-point of summer and its setting-point."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests﴾, he said: "The shortest rising-point in the year and the longest rising-point in the year, and the shortest setting-point in the year and the longest setting-point in the year."

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

That is: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, would you deny, from among these blessings He has bestowed upon you, by His subjecting the sun for you in these two risings and two settings, running for both of you constantly for your benefit and for the welfare of your worldly life and your livelihood?

* *

And His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Lord of the two Easts and the Lord of the two Wests released the two seas, meeting side by side. By His words ﴿released (maraja)﴾ is meant: sent forth and let loose, from the saying: "Fulan released his beast (marraja fulan dabbatahu)" when he let it loose and left it.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas﴾, he says: "He sent forth."

The people of knowledge differed concerning the two seas mentioned by Allah, may His praise be exalted, in this verse: which two seas are they? Some said: They are two seas: one in the heaven and the other on the earth.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side * Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and a sea on the earth."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and a sea on the earth."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "A sea in the heaven and in the earth, meeting each year."

Others said: What is meant is the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad, client of Mus'ab, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "The Sea of Rome, and the Sea of Persia and Yemen."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾: "The two seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, he said: "The Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome."

The most correct of the sayings in my view is the saying of those who said: What is meant is the sea of the heaven and the sea of the earth, because Allah said: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, and pearls and coral come forth only from the shells of the sea of the earth, from the drops of rain of the heaven. So it is known that this refers to the sea of the earth and the sea of the heaven.

* *

And His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Between them is a partition and a separation, so that neither of them corrupts the other, and so that neither transgresses against the other by that. Among the Arabs, everything that lies between two things is a barrier (barzakh), and what lies between this world and the Hereafter is a barzakh.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses against the other."

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "Between them is a partition from Allah, so neither transgresses against the other."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he says: "A partition."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, and the barzakh: "This island, this dry land."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "The barzakh between them is the land that lies between them."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "The salt is restrained from the sweet, and the sweet from the salt, and the water from the dry land, and the dry land from the water, so that neither of them transgresses upon the other by its strength, its subtlety and its power."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side * Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "He prevented them from meeting by the barrier He placed between them from the earth." He said: "The barzakh is what lies beyond the land which He placed between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾. Some said: The meaning of that is: neither of them transgresses against the other.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses against the other."

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that they do not mix.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾, he said: "They do not mix."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they do not transgress upon the dry land.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Upon the dry land. Whatever one takes from the other is transgression, so Allah restrains each from the other by His power, subtlety and majesty, blessed and exalted is He."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: they do not transgress by meeting.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿which they do not transgress﴾: "Neither of them transgresses by wanting to meet its companion."

The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in my view, is to say: Allah described the two seas mentioned in this verse as not transgressing, and He did not restrict their description to one thing rather than another, but made the report about them general. So the correct approach is to generalize it as Allah, exalted is His praise, generalized it: it is said that they do not transgress upon anything, neither does one of them transgress upon the other, nor do they exceed the limit which Allah has set for them.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So which of the blessings of Allah your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, would you deny, from among these blessings He has bestowed upon you, by His releasing the two seas, until He made for you by that an adornment which you wear.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verses 22–25:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ (22) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ (23) ﴿And His are the ships, lofty in the sea like landmarks﴾ (24) ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ (25)

Exalted is He, says: From these two seas, which God has let loose [to meet] and placed between them a barrier, come forth the pearl and the coral. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the description of the pearl and the coral. Some of them said: the pearl is what is large of the pearls, and the coral is what is small of them.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿the pearl and the coral﴾, he said: the pearl: the large ones.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾: as for the pearl, its large ones; and as for the coral, its small ones. Indeed God has in both a treasury to which the common people of Adam's descendants have been guided; they bring forth goods, benefit and adornment, and it reaches its term.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, he said: the pearl: the large pearls; and the coral: the small ones of it.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿the pearl and the coral﴾: as for the coral, it is the small pearls; and as for the pearl, it is what is large of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, he said: the pearl: what is large of it, and the coral: the pearls and the small ones.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: the coral is the small pearls.

- Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Bashshar al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Maysarah al-Harrani related to us, saying: a shaykh in Mecca from the people of Syria related to me, that he heard Ka'b al-Ahbar being asked about the coral, and he said: it is the basadh (a type of precious stone).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: the basadh has veins (shu'ab), and it is better than the pearl.

Others said: the coral among the pearls is the large ones, and the pearl among them is the small ones.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Abi A'ishah, or Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, who said: the coral: the large pearls.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: the coral, he said: what is large of the pearl.

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar related to us, saying: Zuhayr related to us, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ali and from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the coral: the great pearl.

Others said: the coral is the choice pearl.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Musa ibn Abi A'ishah, who said: I asked Murrah about the pearl and the coral, and he said: the coral is the choice pearl.

Others said: the coral is a stone.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Ibn Mas'ud, ﴿the pearl and the coral﴾, he said: the coral is a stone.

The correct view regarding the pearl is that it is what people know, which comes forth from the shells of the sea, from the seed (habb), and as for the coral, I have seen that the people of knowledge of the Arabic language do not dispute that it is the plural of marjanah, and that it is the small pearls. We have already mentioned the differences among the early scholars, and God knows best the correct view.

Some grammarians have claimed that the pearl and the coral come forth from one of the two seas, but it was said "from them" (both), just as one says "I ate bread and milk," and as it is said:

*And I saw your husband in the battle, girded with a sword and a spear.*

[The verse is among the witnesses of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 323). The author has cited it more than once before; refer to it in volumes (3: 275, 6: 281, 7: 294, 9: 200, 11: 142, and its full explanation in volumes 3 and 11). Al-Farra' recited it here at the words of the Exalted: "and dark-eyed maidens (hur 'in)", and said: The companions of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) read it in the genitive (khafd), and this is the Arabic way, although most readers read it in the nominative, because they were averse to making it that the dark-eyed maidens are circulated among (as servants); so they read it in the nominative, as in your saying: "for them are dark-eyed maidens," or "with them are dark-eyed maidens." The genitive is by making the end of the speech follow its beginning, even if what is good in the beginning is not good at the end. An Arab informed me: "When the beautiful women appear one day, and they arch their eyebrows and their eyes..." The eyes are not arched; rather they are darkened with kohl, so he returned it to the eyebrows, because the meaning is understood. Another informed me: "And I met your husband in battle..." (the verse), and the spear is not girded, so he returned it to the sword. End.]

That is not as he claimed; rather it is as I described before, that it comes forth from the shells of the sea, from the rain of the sky. Therefore it was said: ﴿From them comes forth the pearl﴾, meaning by both of them: the two seas.

It is in this manner of what we have said that the people of interpretation spoke.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah al-Razi, from Sufyan ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the sky rains, the shells open their mouths, and from them comes the pearl.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi related to me, saying: Abu Yahya al-Hammani related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the rain descends from the sky, the shells open and it becomes a pearl.

- Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Ghazzi related to me, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Sufyan mentioned, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the sky rains, the shells open for it, and whatever rain falls into them is a pearl.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Fazari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Karkhi, nephew of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, related to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Asbahani, from Ikrimah, who said: No drop falls from the sky into the sea except that there is a pearl in it, or an ambergris plant grows by it, as al-Tabari thinks.

The readers differed in reading His words: ﴿From them comes forth the pearl and the coral﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read ﴿yakhruju﴾ in the form of the passive voice (what has not named its agent). The majority of the readers of Kufa and some of the Meccans read it with a fatha on the ya'.

The correct view regarding this is that they are two well-known readings, and whichever one the reader recites is correct, since their meanings are close.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Exalted is He, says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O two groups (men and jinn), which He has bestowed upon you in what He has brought forth for you from the benefits of these two seas, will you deny?

* *

And His words: ﴿And His are the ships (al-jawari) lofty in the sea﴾

Exalted is He, says: And to the Lord of the two easts and the two wests belong the al-jawari, which are the ships running in the seas.

* *

And His words: ﴿al-munshatu fi al-bahr (lofty in the sea)﴾

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿al-munshi'at﴾ with a kasra on the shin, meaning: the clearly moving ones, which advance and retreat. The majority of the readers of Basra and Medina and some Kufans read ﴿al-munsha'at﴾ with a fatha on the shin, meaning: the raised sails, by which they advance and retreat.

The correct view regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, both correct in meaning and close to each other, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.

Those who spoke regarding the interpretation of this, [said] what we have mentioned:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿al-munsha'at fi al-bahr﴾, he said: whatever ship has its sail raised is munsha'at, and when its sail is not raised it is not munsha'ah.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾, meaning: the ships.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾: meaning: the ships.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾, he said: the ships.

* *

And His words: ﴿like landmarks (al-a'lam)﴾

He says: like mountains; He likened the ships to mountains, and the Arabs call every long mountain an 'alam, and from it is the saying of Jarir:

*When we crossed a landmark, there appeared another landmark...*

[This verse is from a qit'ah in rajaz meter by Jarir al-Khatafi (his Diwan, 520), and its completion is: "until you reach us at al-Hakam." He praises al-Hakam ibn Ayyub al-Thaqafi, the son-in-law and cousin of al-Hajjaj. He describes the she-camels that carried him to him, and therefore we prefer the reading "qata'na" with the feminine plural nun over the reading "qata'na" with the masculine plural pronoun, although the latter is permissible in meaning. Al-a'lam is the plural of 'alam, which is the long mountain; it was named 'alam because the traveller makes it a sign and indication for the road. Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 173-1) and said: "like al-a'lam": like mountains. Jarir said describing camels: "When they crossed..." (the verse).]

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Exalted is He, says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, which He has bestowed upon you, by His running of the al-jawari, the ships which run in the sea for your benefit, will you deny?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verses 22–25:

Others said: the coral among the pearls is the large ones, and the pearl among them is the small ones.

Others said: the coral is the choice pearl.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Musa ibn Abi A'ishah, who said: I asked Murrah about the pearl and the coral, and he said: the coral is the choice pearl.

Others said: the coral is a stone.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Musa ibn Abi A'ishah, who said: I asked Murrah about the pearl and the coral, and he said: the coral is the choice pearl.

Others said: the coral is a stone.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Ibn Mas'ud, ﴿the pearl and the coral﴾, he said: the coral is a stone.

The correct view regarding the pearl is that it is what people know, which comes forth from the shells of the sea, from the seed (habb), and as for the coral, I have seen that the people of knowledge of the Arabic language do not dispute that it is the plural of marjanah, and that it is the small pearls. We have already mentioned the differences among the early scholars, and God knows best the correct view.

Some grammarians have claimed that the pearl and the coral come forth from one of the two seas, but it was said "from them" (both), just as one says "I ate bread and milk," and as it is said:

*And I saw your husband in the battle, girded with a sword and a spear.*

[The verse is among the witnesses of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 323). The author has cited it more than once before; refer to it in volumes (3: 275, 6: 281, 7: 294, 9: 200, 11: 142, and its full explanation in volumes 3 and 11). Al-Farra' recited it here at the words of the Exalted: "and dark-eyed maidens (hur 'in)", and said: The companions of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) read it in the genitive (khafd), and this is the Arabic way, although most readers read it in the nominative, because they were averse to making it that the dark-eyed maidens are circulated among (as servants); so they read it in the nominative, as in your saying: "for them are dark-eyed maidens," or "with them are dark-eyed maidens." The genitive is by making the end of the speech follow its beginning, even if what is good in the beginning is not good at the end. An Arab informed me: "When the beautiful women appear one day, and they arch their eyebrows and their eyes..." The eyes are not arched; rather they are darkened with kohl, so he returned it to the eyebrows, because the meaning is understood. Another informed me: "And I met your husband in battle..." (the verse), and the spear is not girded, so he returned it to the sword. End.]

That is not as he claimed; rather it is as I described before, that it comes forth from the shells of the sea, from the rain of the sky. Therefore it was said: ﴿From them comes forth the pearl﴾, meaning by both of them: the two seas.

It is in this manner of what we have said that the people of interpretation spoke.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah al-Razi, from Sufyan ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the sky rains, the shells open their mouths, and from them comes the pearl.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi related to me, saying: Abu Yahya al-Hammani related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the rain descends from the sky, the shells open and it becomes a pearl.

- Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Ghazzi related to me, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Sufyan mentioned, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Abdullah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the sky rains, the shells open for it, and whatever rain falls into them is a pearl.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Fazari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Karkhi, nephew of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, related to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Asbahani, from Ikrimah, who said: No drop falls from the sky into the sea except that there is a pearl in it, or an ambergris plant grows by it, as al-Tabari thinks.

The readers differed in reading His words: ﴿From them comes forth the pearl and the coral﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read ﴿yakhruju﴾ in the form of the passive voice (what has not named its agent). The majority of the readers of Kufa and some of the Meccans read it with a fatha on the ya'.

The correct view regarding this is that they are two well-known readings, and whichever one the reader recites is correct, since their meanings are close.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Exalted is He, says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O two groups (men and jinn), which He has bestowed upon you in what He has brought forth for you from the benefits of these two seas, will you deny?

* *

And His words: ﴿And His are the ships (al-jawari) lofty in the sea﴾

Exalted is He, says: And to the Lord of the two easts and the two wests belong the al-jawari, which are the ships running in the seas.

* *

And His words: ﴿al-munshatu fi al-bahr (lofty in the sea)﴾

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿al-munshi'at﴾ with a kasra on the shin, meaning: the clearly moving ones, which advance and retreat. The majority of the readers of Basra and Medina and some Kufans read ﴿al-munsha'at﴾ with a fatha on the shin, meaning: the raised sails, by which they advance and retreat.

The correct view regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, both correct in meaning and close to each other, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.

Those who spoke regarding the interpretation of this, [said] what we have mentioned:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿al-munsha'at fi al-bahr﴾, he said: whatever ship has its sail raised is munsha'at, and when its sail is not raised it is not munsha'ah.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾, meaning: the ships.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾: meaning: the ships.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And His are the al-jawari, lofty in the sea, like landmarks﴾, he said: the ships.

* *

And His words: ﴿like landmarks (al-a'lam)﴾

He says: like mountains; He likened the ships to mountains, and the Arabs call every long mountain an 'alam, and from it is the saying of Jarir:

*When we crossed a landmark, there appeared another landmark...*

[This verse is from a qit'ah in rajaz meter by Jarir al-Khatafi (his Diwan, 520), and its completion is: "until you reach us at al-Hakam." He praises al-Hakam ibn Ayyub al-Thaqafi, the son-in-law and cousin of al-Hajjaj. He describes the she-camels that carried him to him, and therefore we prefer the reading "qata'na" with the feminine plural nun over the reading "qata'na" with the masculine plural pronoun, although the latter is permissible in meaning. Al-a'lam is the plural of 'alam, which is the long mountain; it was named 'alam because the traveller makes it a sign and indication for the road. Abu Ubaydah cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 173-1) and said: "like al-a'lam": like mountains. Jarir said describing camels: "When they crossed..." (the verse).]

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Exalted is He, says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, which He has bestowed upon you, by His running of the al-jawari, the ships which run in the sea for your benefit, will you deny?

The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish. And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in a matter. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: everyone upon the earth, of jinn and humankind, will perish. And there will remain the Face of your Lord, O Muhammad, Owner of Majesty and Honour. "Owner of Majesty and Honour" is a description of the Face, which is why ﻿ذو (dhu) is in the nominative case. It has been reported that in the recitation of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), it is read ﴿ذي الجَلال والإكْرام﴾ (dhi al-jalal wa al-ikram) with a ya', as a description of the Lord and an attribute of Him.

* *

His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, O two groups (thaqalan: jinn and humankind), would you deny from among these blessings?

* *

His words: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: To Him turns, seeking the fulfilment of needs, everyone who is in the heavens and the earth, from angels, humans, jinn and others. None of them is independent of Him.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in a matter﴾: The people of the heavens and the people of the earth cannot do without Him. He gives life to the living, causes the dead to die, nurtures the young, and humbles the great. He is the one asked for the needs of the righteous, the final resort of their complaints, and the refuge of the good.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in a matter﴾: He said: It means the asking of His servants of Him for sustenance, death and life; every day He is in that.

* *

His words: ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Every day He is in the matter of His creation, so He relieves the distress of one in distress, raises some people, lowers others, and other affairs of His creation.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, the people of interpretation) said what we have said in this regard.

On the interpretation of His saying, "We will surely attend to you, O you two burdens (al-thaqalan)" [55:31]:

The reciters differed over His saying "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan." The reciters of Medina and Basra in general, and some of the Meccans, read "sanafrughu lakum" with a nun (we). The reciters of Kufa in general read "sayafrughu lakum" with a ya' (He) and a fatha on it, in response to His saying "whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him" [55:29], where it does not say "asks us whoever is in the heavens," so they made the report follow the report.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

As for its interpretation: it is a warning from God to His servants and a threat, like the words of one who threatens and warns another while having no preoccupation that would keep him from punishing him: "I will surely deal with you, and I will attend to you," meaning: I will apply myself to your affair and punish you. One may also say to one who has no occupation: "He has become free for me" and "He has become free for my abuse," meaning he has taken up the matter and turned to it. Likewise His saying, mighty is His praise: "sanafrughu lakum" means: We will call you to account and take up your affair, O humankind and jinn, punishing the people of disobedience and rewarding the people of obedience.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said. Whoever said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan": he said, it is a warning from God to the servants, and God has no preoccupation; He is free.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that he recited "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan" and said: it is near to God, a freedom for His creation.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan," he said: it is a warning; it may also be understood as: We will attend to you concerning what We have promised you of reward and punishment.

And His saying: "Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?" [55:32]

Meaning: Then which of the blessings of your Lord, O two burdens, which He has bestowed upon you, through His reward for the people of His obedience and His punishment for the people of His disobedience, will you deny?

And His saying: "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority" [55:33]

The interpreters differed over the meaning of His saying "if you are able to pass." Some of them said: The meaning is: if you are able to traverse the extremities of the heavens and the earth, and thus overcome your Lord so that He cannot master you, then traverse them, for you will not traverse them except by authority from your Lord. They said: this is said to them on the Day of Resurrection. They said: the sense is: "We will attend to you, O two burdens," and then it is said to them, "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass."

Whoever said that:

- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven, and it splits open with its inhabitants, and those of the angels in it descend and surround the earth and those upon it with the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they stand in rows, one row behind another. Then the highest King descends upon His left flank, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, and they do not come to any region of the earth but find seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. That is the saying of God, 'Indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling, the day you turn your backs fleeing' [40:32–33]. And that is His saying: 'And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and on that day Hell is brought forward' [89:22–23], and His saying: 'O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority' [55:33]. And that is His saying: 'And the sky is split open, for it will be on that day frail, and the angels will be upon its edges' [69:16–17]."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: that you pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass fleeing from death, for death will overtake you, and your fleeing from it will not benefit you.

Whoever said that:

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding "O assembly of jinn and humankind..." to the end of the verse, that it means no one can protect them from death; they are mortal and cannot flee from it or escape it. Even if they passed beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, they would be within God's authority, and God would seize them with death.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it.

Whoever said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority": he said, if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it; you will not know it except by authority, meaning the clear proof from God, mighty is His praise.

Others said: the meaning of His saying "you will not pass" is: you will not go out of My authority.

Whoever said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "you will not pass except by authority": he said, you will not go out of My authority.

As for "al-aqtar" (the regions), it is the plural of "qutr," meaning the extremities.

As related to us by Ibn Humayd, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding "if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth," he said: from their extremities.

And His mighty saying: "And if it had been entered upon them from its regions" [33:14], meaning: from its extremities.

As for His saying "except by authority" (sultan), the interpreters differed over its meaning. Some said it means: except by clear proof, which we have mentioned before.

Others said it means: except by argument.

Whoever said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Ikrimah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority": he said, everything in the Qur'an called "sultan" is "hujjah" (proof).
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "by authority," he said: by proof.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: except by dominion, and you have no dominion.

Whoever said that:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "then pass; you will not pass except by authority": he said, you will not pass except by dominion, and you have no dominion.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority": he said, except by authority from God, except by sovereignty from Him.
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority," meaning: except by sovereignty from God.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: the meaning is: except by argument and proof, for that is the meaning of "sultan" in the speech of the Arabs, though dominion may enter into it, since dominion is a proof.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then which of the blessings of your Lord, O two burdens, which He has bestowed upon you, will you deny, namely the equality among all of you, so that none of you can oppose a command He wills for you?

The reciters of Kufa in general read "sayafrughu lakum" with a ya' (He) and a fatha on it, in response to His saying "whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him" [55:29], where it does not say "asks us whoever is in the heavens," so they made the report follow the report.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

As for its interpretation: it is a warning from God to His servants and a threat, like the words of one who threatens and warns another while having no preoccupation that would keep him from punishing him: "I will surely deal with you, and I will attend to you," meaning: I will apply myself to your affair and punish you. One may also say to one who has no occupation: "He has become free for me" and "He has become free for my abuse," meaning he has taken up the matter and turned to it. Likewise His saying, mighty is His praise: "sanafrughu lakum" means: We will call you to account and take up your affair, O humankind and jinn, punishing the people of disobedience and rewarding the people of obedience.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said. Whoever said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan": he said, it is a warning from God to the servants, and God has no preoccupation; He is free.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that he recited "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan" and said: it is near to God, a freedom for His creation.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding "sanafrughu lakum ayyuha al-thaqalan," he said: it is a warning; it may also be understood as: We will attend to you concerning what We have promised you of reward and punishment.

And His saying: "Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?" [55:32]

Meaning: Then which of the blessings of your Lord, O two burdens, which He has bestowed upon you, through His reward for the people of His obedience and His punishment for the people of His disobedience, will you deny?

And His saying: "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority" [55:33]

The interpreters differed over the meaning of His saying "if you are able to pass." Some of them said: The meaning is: if you are able to traverse the extremities of the heavens and the earth, and thus overcome your Lord so that He cannot master you, then traverse them, for you will not traverse them except by authority from your Lord. They said: this is said to them on the Day of Resurrection. They said: the sense is: "We will attend to you, O two burdens," and then it is said to them, "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass."

Whoever said that:

- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven, and it splits open with its inhabitants, and those of the angels in it descend and surround the earth and those upon it with the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they stand in rows, one row behind another. Then the highest King descends upon His left flank, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, and they do not come to any region of the earth but find seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. That is the saying of God, 'Indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling, the day you turn your backs fleeing' [40:32–33]. And that is His saying: 'And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and on that day Hell is brought forward' [89:22–23], and His saying: 'O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority' [55:33]. And that is His saying: 'And the sky is split open, for it will be on that day frail, and the angels will be upon its edges' [69:16–17]."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: that you pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass fleeing from death, for death will overtake you, and your fleeing from it will not benefit you.

Whoever said that:

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding "O assembly of jinn and humankind..." to the end of the verse, that it means no one can protect them from death; they are mortal and cannot flee from it or escape it. Even if they passed beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, they would be within God's authority, and God would seize them with death.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it.

Whoever said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except by authority": he said, if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it; you will not know it except by authority, meaning the clear proof from God, mighty is His praise.

Others said: the meaning of His saying "you will not pass" is: you will not go out of My authority.

Whoever said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "you will not pass except by authority": he said, you will not go out of My authority.

As for "al-aqtar" (the regions), it is the plural of "qutr," meaning the extremities.

As related to us by Ibn Humayd, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding "if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth," he said: from their extremities.

And His mighty saying: "And if it had been entered upon them from its regions" [33:14], meaning: from its extremities.

As for His saying "except by authority" (sultan), the interpreters differed over its meaning. Some said it means: except by clear proof, which we have mentioned before.

Others said it means: except by argument.

Whoever said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Ikrimah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority": he said, everything in the Qur'an called "sultan" is "hujjah" (proof).
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "by authority," he said: by proof.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: except by dominion, and you have no dominion.

Whoever said that:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "then pass; you will not pass except by authority": he said, you will not pass except by dominion, and you have no dominion.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority": he said, except by authority from God, except by sovereignty from Him.
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "you will not pass except by authority," meaning: except by sovereignty from God.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: the meaning is: except by argument and proof, for that is the meaning of "sultan" in the speech of the Arabs, though dominion may enter into it, since dominion is a proof.

And His saying: "Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?" [55:34]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then which of the blessings of your Lord, O two burdens, which He has bestowed upon you, will you deny, namely the equality among all of you, so that none of you can oppose a command He wills for you?

On the interpretation of His words, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves (35). So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny? (36) And when the sky splits open and becomes red like rose-coloured leather (37). So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny? (38)"

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "There will be sent against you both," O you two weights (mankind and jinn) on the Day of Resurrection, "a flame of fire," meaning its blaze, from where it kindles and is set ablaze, without any smoke in it. Among the poetic uses of this is the verse of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"Indeed for them from our onslaught are cauldrons, and a war-fire that kindles the shuwaz."

[The two verses are in the Diwan of al-'Ajjaj (Leipzig edition, p. 81), and in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah (folio 173), where the poet's name is not given. He said, at the words of the Exalted (There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass): shuwaz (with the first letter vowelled with a damma) and shiwaz (with the first letter vowelled with a kasra) (the pen-vowelling): the singular, which is the fire that blazes without smoke.

He said: "Indeed for them from our onslaught..." the two verses. In al-Lisan (root sh-w-z-), "al-shuwaz" and "al-shawaz" (with the first vowelled with a damma and the second with a kasra) are the flame that has no smoke. Ru'bah said: "Indeed for them..." the two verses. In the Mighty Revelation: "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass." Al-Farra' said: most of the readers recited shuwaz with a damma, while al-Hasan recited it with a kasra on the shin, as they say for a herd of cattle, siwar and sawar. End of quote.]

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "shuwaz min nar" (a flame of fire): he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "shuwaz min nar": he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the scattered blaze. [Al-mutaqatti': so it is in the original, and so it is in al-Shawkani (5:134).]

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is this green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak: "al-shuwaz": the flame.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": i.e., a flame of fire.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, "shuwaz min nar": he said: a flame of fire.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the flame; as for the brass, Allah knows best what He intended by it.

Those who said so:

And others said: the shuwaz is the smoke that comes out of the flame.

Those who said so:

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "shuwaz min nar": the smoke that comes out of the flame, not the smoke of firewood.

The readers differed in reciting His words "shuwaz." The majority of the readers of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah recited it with a damma on the shin, except Ibn Abi Ishaq, while Ibn Abi Ishaq and 'Abdullah ibn Kathir recited "shiwaz min nar" with a kasra on the shin. Both are dialects, like "al-sawar" for a herd of cattle, and "al-sawar" with a kasra or damma on the sad. The recitation I prefer of the two is the damma on the shin, because it is the well-known dialect, and it is also the recitation of the readers of the provinces.

As for His words "wa nuhas," the interpreters differed about what is meant by it. Some of them said: it means smoke.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: Musa ibn 'Umayr related to us, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "wa nuhasun fala tantasirani": he said: the nuhas is smoke.

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "wa nuhas": the smoke of the fire.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words "wa nuhas": he said: smoke.

And others said: what is meant by nuhas in this place is the copper (sufr).

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, "wa nuhas": he said: the nuhas is the copper (sufr) with which they will be punished.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "wa nuhas": he said: the copper is melted and poured over their heads.

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "wa nuhas": he said: the copper is melted and poured on his head.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, "wa nuhas": the copper is melted and poured over their heads.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, "wa nuhas": he said: He threatened them with copper, by which, as you hear, He will punish them.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam related to us, from Qatadah, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass": he said: He threatens them with fire and with brass.

The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: what is meant by nuhas is smoke. That is because He, may His majesty be exalted, mentioned that a flame of fire would be sent against these two groups, which is pure fire not mixed with smoke. What is more fitting to the context is that He threatened them with a fire of this description, and that the threat be followed by something of the same kind but different from it, not something of another kind, and that is smoke. The Arabs call smoke nuhas, with a damma on the nun and with a kasra on it, and the readers are unanimous on the damma. Among the uses of nuhas in the sense of smoke is the verse of Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan: "It shines like the light of a lamp of... Allah did not place in it any nuhas." [The verse belongs to Nabigha of Banu Ju'dah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 173b), and the copyist garbled his name, so he said "like Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan" in this author's commentary. Abu 'Ubaydah said at the words "wa nuhas": nuhas and nuhas (vowelled with a damma and kasra on the first letter, pen-vowelling), and al-nuhas is smoke. Nabigha of Banu Ju'dah said: "It shines..." the verse; and at its beginning it reads tudi' with a ya', not a waw, as the copyist of the commentary wrote it. (In al-Lisan, root d-w-'.) Sarraja al-siraj yadu', and ada'a yudi'. He said: the second dialect is the chosen one. End of quote.]

That is, smoke.

As for His words, "fala tantasirani" (so you will not be able to defend yourselves):

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: you will not be able to defend yourselves, O jinn and mankind, against it when He punishes you with this punishment, and you will not be rescued from it.

As related:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, "fala tantasirani": he said: meaning the jinn and mankind.

He said: As for His words, "fa-idha inshaqqati al-sama'u fa-kanat wardatan ka-l-dihan" (And when the sky splits open and becomes red like rose-coloured leather): Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: when the sky splits and is rent asunder, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, its colour will be the colour of a red-rose-coloured horse.

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

- Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt related to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, "fa-kanat wardatan ka-l-dihan": he said: like a rose-coloured horse.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words "fa-idha inshaqqati al-sama'u fa-kanat wardatan ka-l-dihan": he said: its colour changes.

- 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hayawiyah related to us, saying: Shihab ibn 'Abbad related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Humayd related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His words "wardatan ka-l-dihan": he said: like the colour of the rose-coloured horse, and then afterwards it became like leather.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words "wardatan ka-l-dihan": he said: like oil.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "ka-l-dihan": he means: pure.

And others said: what is meant by it is: "fa-kanat wardatan ka-l-adim" (it became red like tanned leather), and they said: al-dihan is plural, its singular being dahn.

The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: what is meant by it is oil, in the brightness of its colour, because that is the known usage in the speech of the Arabs.

* *

As for His words, "fa-bi-ayyi alai rabbikuma tukadhdhibani" (So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?):

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: By which power of your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, do you deny, concerning what He has informed you that He will do to you?

On the interpretation of His words, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves (35). So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny? (36) And when the sky splits open and becomes red like rose-coloured leather (37). So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny? (38)"

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "There will be sent against you both," O you two weights (mankind and jinn) on the Day of Resurrection, "a flame of fire," meaning its blaze, from where it kindles and is set ablaze, without any smoke in it. Among the poetic uses of this is the verse of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"Indeed for them from our onslaught are cauldrons, and a war-fire that kindles the shuwaz."

[The two verses are in the Diwan of al-'Ajjaj (Leipzig edition, p. 81), and in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah (folio 173), where the poet's name is not given. He said, at the words of the Exalted (There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass): shuwaz (with the first letter vowelled with a damma) and shiwaz (with the first letter vowelled with a kasra) (the pen-vowelling): the singular, which is the fire that blazes without smoke.

He said: "Indeed for them from our onslaught..." the two verses. In al-Lisan (root sh-w-z-), "al-shuwaz" and "al-shawaz" (with the first vowelled with a damma and the second with a kasra) are the flame that has no smoke. Ru'bah said: "Indeed for them..." the two verses. In the Mighty Revelation: "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass." Al-Farra' said: most of the readers recited shuwaz with a damma, while al-Hasan recited it with a kasra on the shin, as they say for a herd of cattle, siwar and sawar. End of quote.]

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "shuwaz min nar" (a flame of fire): he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "shuwaz min nar": he said: the blaze of the fire.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the scattered blaze. [Al-mutaqatti': so it is in the original, and so it is in al-Shawkani (5:134).]

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is this green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the green, scattered flame of fire.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak: "al-shuwaz": the flame.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": i.e., a flame of fire.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, "shuwaz min nar": he said: a flame of fire.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire": he said: the shuwaz is the flame; as for the brass, Allah knows best what He intended by it.

Those who said so:

And others said: the shuwaz is the smoke that comes out of the flame.

Those who said so:

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "shuwaz min nar": the smoke that comes out of the flame, not the smoke of firewood.

The readers differed in reciting His words "shuwaz." The majority of the readers of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah recited it with a damma on the shin, except Ibn Abi Ishaq, while Ibn Abi Ishaq and 'Abdullah ibn Kathir recited "shiwaz min nar" with a kasra on the shin. Both are dialects, like "al-sawar" for a herd of cattle, and "al-sawar" with a kasra or damma on the sad. The recitation I prefer of the two is the damma on the shin, because it is the well-known dialect, and it is also the recitation of the readers of the provinces.

As for His words "wa nuhas," the interpreters differed about what is meant by it. Some of them said: it means smoke.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: Musa ibn 'Umayr related to us, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "wa nuhasun fala tantasirani": he said: the nuhas is smoke.

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "wa nuhas": the smoke of the fire.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words "wa nuhas": he said: smoke.

And others said: what is meant by nuhas in this place is the copper (sufr).

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, "wa nuhas": he said: the nuhas is the copper (sufr) with which they will be punished.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "wa nuhas": he said: the copper is melted and poured over their heads.

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, "wa nuhas": he said: the copper is melted and poured on his head.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, "wa nuhas": the copper is melted and poured over their heads.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, "wa nuhas": he said: He threatened them with copper, by which, as you hear, He will punish them.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam related to us, from Qatadah, "There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and brass": he said: He threatens them with fire and with brass.

The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: what is meant by nuhas is smoke. That is because He, may His majesty be exalted, mentioned that a flame of fire would be sent against these two groups, which is pure fire not mixed with smoke. What is more fitting to the context is that He threatened them with a fire of this description, and that the threat be followed by something of the same kind but different from it, not something of another kind, and that is smoke. The Arabs call smoke nuhas, with a damma on the nun and with a kasra on it, and the readers are unanimous on the damma. Among the uses of nuhas in the sense of smoke is the verse of Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan: "It shines like the light of a lamp of... Allah did not place in it any nuhas." [The verse belongs to Nabigha of Banu Ju'dah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 173b), and the copyist garbled his name, so he said "like Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan" in this author's commentary. Abu 'Ubaydah said at the words "wa nuhas": nuhas and nuhas (vowelled with a damma and kasra on the first letter, pen-vowelling), and al-nuhas is smoke. Nabigha of Banu Ju'dah said: "It shines..." the verse; and at its beginning it reads tudi' with a ya', not a waw, as the copyist of the commentary wrote it. (In al-Lisan, root d-w-'.) Sarraja al-siraj yadu', and ada'a yudi'. He said: the second dialect is the chosen one. End of quote.]

That is, smoke.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 39–42:**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ ﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾ ﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: On that Day the angels will not question the criminals about their sins, because God has preserved them against those sins, and their Lord will not question some of them about the sins of others.

Something similar to what we have said has been said by the people of ta'wil (the scholars of Qur'anic interpretation).

Among those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: He will not question them about their deeds, and they will not question one another. This is like His words: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾ (28:78), and like His words to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Hellfire﴾ (2:119).

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He said: God, mighty and majestic, has preserved their deeds against them.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He said: There was questioning, then a seal was placed on the mouths of the people, and their hands and feet speak of what they used to do.
