Something similar to what we have said has been said by the people of ta'wil (the scholars of Qur'anic interpretation).

Among those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: He will not question them about their deeds, and they will not question one another. This is like His words: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾ (28:78), and like His words to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Hellfire﴾ (2:119).

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He said: God, mighty and majestic, has preserved their deeds against them.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He said: Mujahid used to say: The angels will not question the criminals, who are recognized by their marks.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, and said: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾. He said: There was questioning, then a seal was placed on the mouths of the people, and their hands and feet speak of what they used to do.

* * *

And His words: ﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O you two groups (al-thaqalan, humankind and jinn), will you deny, the favor He has bestowed upon you through His justice toward you, that He does not punish any of you except a criminal?

[[Perhaps the word "tukadhdhibaan" (you deny), which the author used to end such expressions with in what has preceded, fell from the copyist's pen. [The verse reads]: "Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?"]]

* * *

And His words: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: The angels will recognize the criminals by their signs and marks, which God has imprinted on them: blackened faces and blue-tinged eyes.

As:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾. He said: They will be recognized by blackened faces and bluish eyes.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾. He said: Blue eyes, black faces.

* * *

And His words: ﴿and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: The zabaniyah (guardians of Hell) will seize them by their forelocks and feet, dragging them to Hell and hurling them into it.

﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, will you deny, the favor He has bestowed upon you by making His angels recognize the criminals among the people of obedience from among you, so that they alone are singled out for humiliation and disgrace, rather than others.

The explanation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿This is Hellfire, which the criminals deny. They will circulate between it and scalding water, ever-boiling.  So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verses 46–49:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens (46). Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (47) Having branches (48). Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (49)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And for whoever fears God among His servants, fearing his standing before Him, obeying Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobediences, are two gardens", meaning two orchards.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this, although their wording differs in explaining its interpretation; yet the meaning of all of them tends toward this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: God, may His praise be exalted, promised the believers who feared His standing and performed His obligations Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He says: he feared and then was God-conscious, and "the one who fears" is one who engages in obedience to God and abandons His disobedience.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ — it is the man who intends to commit a sin, then remembers the standing before his Lord and refrains.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: the man who intends a sin, then remembers his standing before God and leaves it, for him are two gardens.

He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: the man who intends disobedience, then remembers God, may He be exalted, and leaves it.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: it concerns the one who, when he intends an act of disobedience, abandons it.

Nasr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: it is the man who intends to disobey God, the Exalted, then leaves it out of fear of God.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: he commits a sin, then remembers the standing before his Lord and leaves it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding this verse: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: when he wants to commit a sin, he refrains out of fear of God.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: the believers feared that standing, so they acted for it, submitted to it, and worshipped by night and day.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam related to us, saying: Qatadah related to us, regarding His words: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ He said: God has a standing which the believers feared.

Muhammad ibn Musa related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Jurayri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾. I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals, even if Abu al-Darda's nose is rubbed in the dust."

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, from Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: Abu al-Darda' informed me that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) once recited this verse: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾. I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals, O Messenger of God?" He said: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾. He said: I said: "O Messenger of God, even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 54–55:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Reclining on couches whose linings are of brocade, and the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand (54). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (55)﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ in which they enjoy delight, ﴿reclining on couches﴾. The word "reclining" (muttaki'in) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) relating to the meaning of the preceding statement, because the preceding statement means the report that the one who fears the standing before his Lord is in bounty and joy, enjoying delight in the two gardens.

* *

And His saying: ﴿on couches whose linings are of brocade, and the fruit of the two gardens﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: the linings of these couches are of thick brocade (dibaj). Al-istabraq (thick brocade) among the Arabs is what is thick and coarse of brocade.

Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from among the people of Basra used to say: any fabric that is neither as thick as brocade nor as light as ʿaraqa is called istabraq.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

* Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Saʿid narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah said to me: "What is istabraq?" He said: I said: "What is thick and coarse of brocade."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi ʿArubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿istabraq﴾, he said: thick brocade.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Zayd al-Khattabi narrated to us, he said: al-Firyabi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarim, from Ibn Masʿud regarding His saying: ﴿couches whose linings are of brocade﴾, he said: "You have been told about the linings; how would it be if you were told about the outer surfaces?"

⁕ al-Rifaʿi narrated to us, he said: Ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayrah, he said: "These are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces?"

⁕ Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Yaʿqub, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, he said: It was said to him: "These linings are of istabraq, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: "This is of what God said: ﴿no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾." The grammarians of Arabic have claimed that the lining may be the outer side and the outer side may be the lining, because each of them may be the face. He said: The Arabs say: "This is the back (zahr) of the sky" and "this is the belly (batn) of the sky," meaning its visible outer side that we see.

And His saying: ﴿and the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾

He says: the fruit of the two gardens that is picked is near to them, because they do not toil by climbing their palms and trees to pick its fruit, but they pick it while seated, without hardship.

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: "Their fruits are near; neither distance nor thorns keep their hands from it." It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no man will pluck a fruit from Paradise and bring it to his mouth until God replaces it with something better than it."

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿and the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾, he said: "Neither distance nor thorns keep his hand back."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verses 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾ [56], ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [57]

He, exalted is His mention, says: In these couches whose linings are of brocade, ﴿restraining their gaze﴾, and they are the women whose gaze has been restricted to their husbands, so they do not look at other men.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾, he said: Their gaze is restricted from men, so they look only at their husbands.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾ ... the verse, he said: Their gaze is restricted to their husbands, so they do not desire others.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿restraining their gaze﴾: They look only at their husbands. [She] says: "By the might of my Lord, His majesty and His beauty, I see in Paradise nothing more beautiful than you. Praise be to God who made you my husband and made me your wife."

* *

And His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾

He says: No man has touched them before these whose qualities He, exalted is His praise, has described, and they are the ones of whom He said, ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾. And no jinn. It is said of this: "No rope has ever touched (tamathat) this camel," meaning it has not been touched by a rope.

Some of the scholars of the Arabic language among the Kufans used to say: al-tamth is intercourse accompanied by bleeding, and they said: al-tamth is blood, and they said: "He deflowered her (tamathaha)" when he made her bleed through intercourse.

What is meant in this place is that no man or jinn has had intercourse with them before them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, he said: No man or jinn has deflowered them.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verses 58–61**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾ (58) ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you two deny?﴾ (59) ﴿Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?﴾ (60) ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you two deny?﴾ (61)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those women restraining their gaze, who are in these two gardens, are in their purity like rubies, through which one sees the thread that is in them from behind it. Likewise, the marrow of their shins is seen from behind their bodies, and in their beauty they are like rubies and coral.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of the report transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning this:

- Muhammad ibn Hatim related to me, saying: 'Ubaydah related to us, from Humayd, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen from behind seventy garments of silk, and so is its marrow. That is because God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾. As for the ruby, if you were to insert a thread into it and then strain it, you would see it from behind it."

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise wears seventy garments of silk, and the whiteness of her shin and its beauty are seen from behind them. That is because God says ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾. Surely the ruby is a stone; if you were to insert a thread into it and then strain it, you would look at the thread from behind the stone."

- He said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾: in the whiteness of coral.

- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: 'Abdullah informed us: "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise wears seventy garments of silk, and the whiteness of her shin and its beauty, and the marrow of her shin, are seen from behind that. That is because God said ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾. Do you not see that the ruby is a stone? When you insert a thread into it, you see the thread from behind the stone."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed, a woman of the houris (al-hur al-'in) wears seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin is seen as red drink is seen in a white glass."

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: al-Mutallib ibn Ziyad related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾, he said: the purity of the ruby and the beauty of the coral.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾: the purity of the ruby in the whiteness of coral. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters Paradise, he has in it two wives, whose shin-marrow is seen from behind their garments."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to us, saying: Abu al-'Awwam related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾, he said: their purity was likened to the purity of the ruby in the whiteness of coral.

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾: in the purity of the ruby and the whiteness of coral.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾: "As if they were rubies in purity and coral in whiteness. The purity is the purity of the ruby, and the whiteness is the whiteness of pearl."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾, he said: in the purity of the ruby and the whiteness of coral.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying "and His Throne was upon the water." He said: The Throne of God was upon the water, then He took for Himself a garden, then He took besides it another garden, then He sealed them both with one pearl. He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two gardens﴾, and they are the ones that no soul knows, or he said: and they are the ones that no soul knows what has been concealed for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do. He said: They are the ones that creation does not know what is in them, or what is in it; there comes to them every day from it, or from them both, a gift (tuhfah).

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in similar words.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: besides them both in virtue (al-fadl).

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And besides these two, there are two gardens﴾: They are lesser than these two, for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin).

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿dark green﴾: He says: green-verdant.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿dark green﴾, he said: verdant from irrigation, and it is said: intertwined.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Haritha ibn Sulayman al-Sulami, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr, while he was explaining this verse from the pulpit, saying: Do you know what ﴿dark green﴾ is? Verdant from irrigation.

Muhammad ibn Imara, that is al-Asadi, narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Haritha ibn Sulayman, thus he said: Ibn al-Zubayr said: ﴿dark green﴾: verdant from irrigation.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Ata'iyya: ﴿dark green﴾, he said: verdant from irrigation.

Muhammad ibn Imara narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying ﴿dark green﴾, he said: verdant from irrigation.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr ﴿dark green﴾, he said: irrigation overspread them with blackness and greenness.

He said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr ﴿dark green﴾, he said: verdant.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying ﴿dark green﴾, he said: soft.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan ﴿dark green﴾, he said: blackish from irrigation.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾, he said: They are the gardens of the foremost; then he recited ﴿having branches﴾, and recited ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾; then he returned to the companions of the right and said ﴿And besides these two, there are two gardens﴾, and mentioned their excellence and what is in them. He said: ﴿dark green﴾, from the greenness, from the intensity of their greenness, until they nearly became black.

* *

His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

He says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He has bestowed upon you two by what has been mentioned, will you two deny?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verses 68–71:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿In them are fruit and palm trees and pomegranates (68). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (69) In them are good, beautiful [companions] (70). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (71)﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: In these two gardens of dark green [foliage] are fruit, palm trees and pomegranates.

Scholars have differed over the reason why the palm tree and the pomegranate are mentioned again, given that it has already been said that fruit is in them. Some said: they are repeated because the palm tree and the pomegranate are not [classed as] fruit.

Others said: they are [indeed] fruit. They said: we say they are fruit because the Arabs classify them as fruit. They said: If it is said to us, "How are they repeated when their mention has already passed together with the mention of all the other fruits?", we say: it is like His words: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾. He had commanded them to guard every prayer, then He repeated the afternoon prayer to emphasise it. Likewise, the palm tree and the pomegranate are repeated to encourage the people of Paradise. He said: It is also like His words: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth?﴾, then He said: ﴿and many among mankind, and many deserve the punishment﴾, and He had already mentioned them at the start of the statement in His words: ﴿all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth﴾.

Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The palm trees of Paradise: their trunks are of gold, their roots are of gold, their fronds [kara nif] are of emerald, and their palm fronds are a garment for the people of Paradise. Their dates are like buckets, whiter than milk, softer than butter, sweeter than honey, and have no stone."

He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Wahb al-Dhamari, who said: "It has reached us that in Paradise there are palm trees whose trunks are of gold, whose fronds [kara nif] are of gold, whose leaflets are of gold, and whose palm fronds are a garment for the people of Paradise, the finest robes that people have ever seen. Their spikelets [shamarikh] are of gold, their stalks [araji n] are of gold, their pollen-sheaths [thafarik] are of gold, and their dates are like jars, whiter than milk and silver, sweeter than honey and sugar, and softer than butter and ghee."

As for His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

He says: So which of the blessings of your Lord will you two deny? That is, which of the blessings of your Lord, which He has bestowed upon you, with this honour with which He has honoured the one who does good among you, will you two deny?

* *

As for His words: ﴿In them are good, beautiful [companions]﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: In these four gardens, of which two are for one who fears the standing before his Lord, and the other two, beneath them, are the dark green ones, [there are] good of character and beautiful of face.

His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

The correct view is that the report about them, that they are restrained within pavilions to their husbands so that they do not desire others, is general, just as it has been generalised.

And His words: ﴿within the pavilions (khiyām)﴾

By khiyām is meant: houses. The Arabs may call the litters of women khiyām. From it is the saying of Labid:

Shāqatka ẓaʿn al-ḥayy yawma taḥammalū / fatakannasū quṭnan taṣirru khiyāmuhā [This verse is by Labid; Abu ʿUbayda cited it in Majaz al-Quran (folio 174-1) when explaining the verse: "ḥūr maqṣūrāt fī al-khiyām"; he said: al-ḥawrāʾ: one whose eye-white is very white and eye-black very black. maqṣūrāt: i.e., secluded in the tents. al-khiyām: houses. And also the litters (hawdaj) are khiyām, Labid said: ...]

As for in this verse, it is meant as houses.

The correct reading in this matter is what the readers of the metropolitan cities hold, because it is the eloquent dialect and the well-known speech of the Arabs.

• He said: Waki narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿ḥūr﴾, he said: women.

• I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Maidens, restrained﴾, the ḥawrāʼ: the large-eyed beautiful one.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: the ḥūr: blackness within whiteness.

• He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Maidens, restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: the ḥūr: the white of their hearts, their souls and their eyes.

As for His words ﴿maqṣūrāt (restrained)﴾, the interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its interpretation is that they are restricted to their husbands, so they do not desire any replacement for them, nor do they raise their glances to other men.

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Israʼil informed us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid: ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: their glance and their selves are restricted to their husbands.

• Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid ﴿restrained﴾, he said: their glance is restricted to their husbands, so they do not turn to others.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: they restrict their selves and their glances to their husbands, so they do not turn to others.

• Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah and Ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: they restrict their glance to their husbands.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Mujahid ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: they restrict their selves, their hearts and their glances to their husbands, so they do not turn to others.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: their glance is restricted to their husbands, so they do not turn to others.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿restrained﴾, he said: restricted to their husbands, so they do not turn to others.

Others said: it is meant that they are confined in the curtained litters (ḥijāl).

Mention of those who said that:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah ﴿ḥūr restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: confined in the tents.

• Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Bazuri narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, the like of it.

• Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuaym narrated to us, from Israʼil, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿restrained﴾, he said: confined.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, saying: Abu Maʿshar al-Sindi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, he said: confined in the curtained litters.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: they do not leave the pavilions.

• ʿUbayd ibn Ismaʿil al-Hibari narrated to me, saying: ʿUtham ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, concerning His words: ﴿ḥūr restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: the virgins of Paradise.

• Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham narrated to us, both saying: ʿUtham ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, the like of it.

• I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿restrained﴾, he said: confined in the pavilions, not coming out of them.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: confined, not roaming the roads.

The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted is He, described them as restrained within pavilions, and restraint means confinement. He did not restrict their description as confined to one of the two meanings we have mentioned rather than the other; rather, He made their description general. The correct view is that the report about them, that they are restrained within pavilions to their husbands so that they do not desire others, is general, just as it has been generalised.

* *

And His words: ﴿within the pavilions (khiyām)﴾

By khiyām is meant: houses. The Arabs may call the litters of women khiyām. From it is the saying of Labid:

Shāqatka ẓaʿn al-ḥayy yawma taḥammalū / fatakannasū quṭnan taṣirru khiyāmuhā [This verse is by Labid; Abu ʿUbayda cited it in Majaz al-Quran (folio 174-1) when explaining the verse: "ḥūr maqṣūrāt fī al-khiyām"; he said: al-ḥawrāʾ: one whose eye-white is very white and eye-black very black. maqṣūrāt: i.e., secluded in the tents. al-khiyām: houses. And also the litters (hawdaj) are khiyām, Labid said: ...]

As for in this verse, it is meant as houses.

Interpreters of the Qur'an said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Saʿid, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah: ﴿ḥūr restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: hollow pearl.

• al-Hasan ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

• Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbuʿi narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn ʿIyad narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: ﴿ḥūr restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: the pavilion is a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, having four thousand leaves of gold.

• Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuaym narrated to us, from Israʼil, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿in the pavilions﴾, he said: houses of pearls.

• Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Idris al-Awdi narrated to us, from Shammar ibn ʿAtiyah, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Do you know what "ḥūr restrained within pavilions" means? The pavilions: hollow pearl.

• He said: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Musʿar narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abu al-Ahwas, concerning His words: ﴿ḥūr restrained within pavilions﴾, he said: hollow pearl.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He bestowed upon you, of honour, by rewarding your benefactors with this honour, would you two deny?

* *

And His words: ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before them﴾

He, mentioned is He, says: No human has had intercourse with them, causing them to bleed (yadmithunna), before them, nor any jinn.

The readers of the metropolitan cities recited ﴿lam yaṭmithhunna﴾ with a kasra on the mīm in this place and in the one before it. al-Kisaʾi used to read one of them with a kasra and the other with a ḍamma.

The correct reading in this matter is what the readers of the metropolitan cities hold, because it is the eloquent dialect and the well-known speech of the Arabs.

* *

And His words: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He says: So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He bestowed upon you, of what has been described, would you two deny?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 76–78:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Reclining on green cushions and fine, beautiful carpets (76). So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny? (77) Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor (78)﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: These people whom He, may His praise be exalted, has honored with this honor, which He described in these verses, will be blessed with it in the two gardens which He described, ﴿reclining on green cushions and fine, beautiful carpets﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of al-Rafraf (green cushions). Some of them said: it is the gardens of Paradise, its singular being: rafrafa (a single garden).

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said regarding this verse, ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: the gardens of Paradise.

Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuh narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: al-Rafraf: the gardens of Paradise.

Others said: they are the cushioned seats (al-mahabis).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he says: the mahabis.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: al-Rafraf is the surplus of the mahabis and the bisat (spreads).

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: they are the bisat; the people of Medina say: they are the bisat.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami, from a man called Ghazwan, ﴿green cushions﴾, he said: the surplus of the mahabis.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Harun, from Antara, from his father, he said: the surplus of the furnishings and the mahabis.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Marwan, regarding His saying: ﴿green cushions﴾, he said: the surplus of the mahabis.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: al-Rafraf al-Khudr: the mahabis.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿green cushions﴾, he said: green mahabis.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿green cushions﴾, he said: they are the mahabis.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: al-Rafraf: the mahabis.

Others said: rather, they are the armrests (al-marafiq).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: al-Rafraf: green armrests. As for al-'Abqari, it is the thick rugs, and it is the plural whose singular is 'abqariyya. And it has been mentioned that the Arabs call everything of spreads 'abqari.

It is in accordance with what we have said regarding this that the people of interpretation spoke.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: al-Zarabi.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: al-'Abqari: fine zarabi.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: al-'Abqari: choice zarabi.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: al-'Abqari: the zarabi.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: the zarabi.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: zarabi.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: al-'Abqari: the tanafis (thick rugs).

Others said: al-'Abqari: brocade (al-dibaj).

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mujahid, ﴿and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, he said: it is brocade.

The reciters in all the provinces are in agreement on reciting it as ﴿on green cushions and fine, beautiful carpets﴾, without an alif in both words. It has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ a report that is not preserved and not of sound chain: ﴿'ala rafarifa khudrin wa 'abaqiriyyu﴾ with an alif and with the vowel-ending (al-ijra'). It has been reported from Zuhayr al-Furqubi that he used to recite (ʿalā rafārifa khuḍrin), with an alif and without the vowel-ending, ﴿wa 'abaqiri hisanin﴾ also with an alif, and without the vowel-ending. As for al-rafarif in this reading, it may bear a correct form. As for al-'abaqiri, it has no correct form according to the grammarians of Arabic, because the alif of the plural (alif al-jama') cannot be followed by four letters, nor by three sound letters. As for the first reading that was mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ, if it were sound, the two words would have to be without the vowel-ending.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He has bestowed upon you, from His honoring of the people of obedience among you with this honor, will you deny?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: Blessed is the remembrance of your Lord, O Muhammad, ﴿Owner of Majesty﴾: meaning, Owner of Greatness, ﴿and Honor﴾, meaning: and He to whom honor belongs from among all His creation.

As is related:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Owner of Majesty and Honor﴾, he says: Owner of Greatness and Pride.

End of the commentary on Surat al-Rahman, Exalted and Mighty is He.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 76–78:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Reclining on green cushions and fine, beautiful carpets (76). So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny? (77) Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor (78)﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: These people whom He, may His praise be exalted, has honored with this honor, which He described in these verses, will be blessed with it in the two gardens which He described, ﴿reclining on green cushions and fine, beautiful carpets﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of al-Rafraf (green cushions). Some of them said: it is the gardens of Paradise, its singular being: rafrafa (a single garden).

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said regarding this verse, ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: the gardens of Paradise.

Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuh narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he said: al-Rafraf: the gardens of Paradise.

Others said: they are the cushioned seats (al-mahabis).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿reclining on green cushions﴾, he says: the mahabis.
